subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: John Hargreaves <john.hargreaves@legacybank.com>, Priya Sethi <priya.sethi@legacybank.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi John / Priya — thanks again for the quick call earlier today. Below is a short recap and a list of open items we flagged so we can align next steps.

Recap: 
- Primary goal: run LLM-powered customer support models inside LegacyBank's air-gapped data center to meet regulatory/data residency requirements.
- Deployment mode preference: private on-prem (air-gapped) with HSM KMS integration, occasional offline upgrades via signed artifacts.
- Traffic profile: mostly low-latency inference (payment reference extraction + reranking) with occasional batching for batch jobs.

Open items / questions for qualification (please reply inline where helpful):
1) Hardware specs: what GPU SKUs/host counts do you currently have or plan to procure? We need GPU model, memory, per-node CPU/RAM, and disk type.
2) Throughput: expected concurrent QPS and typical request size (tokens per request) so we can recommend model/replica sizing.
3) Airgap constraints: confirm that nodes have no outbound internet and that software will need to be delivered via USB/secure media + signed artifacts.
4) Offline ops & upgrades: how do you plan to handle kernel/OS/firmware updates? Do you have a maintenance window cadence?
5) Network & bastion access: will we have temporary console/bastion access for initial install and troubleshooting, or does all support need to be screen-shared sessions?

Next steps I propose:
- Please answer the bullets above (1–5).
- Once we have hardware/inventory details, Redwood will propose a suggested POC configuration (2-node POC vs full rack).
- Schedule a technical POC planning call: suggest Tues 6/1 or Wed 6/2, 10–12 PDT.

I've attached a short one-pager with our typical on-prem requirements for air-gapped installs (redwood_onprem_requirements_v1.pdf) for your infra team to review.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call to walk through any item.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: John Hargreaves <john.hargreaves@legacybank.com>

Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 20:03:12 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up

Thanks Marissa — good summary. Answering inline below: 

1) Hardware specs:
- Current footprint: 2 rack units dedicated for AI (we can expand). Planned procurement: 2x appliance nodes initially for POC, each with 3x NVIDIA H100 80GB GPUs (total 6 GPUs) — CPUs: dual 32-core AMD Rome, RAM: 1.5TB per node, local NVMe (8TB), redundant power.
- Full target would be 4 racks (provisioned over time).

2) Throughput:
- Expected steady-state QPS: 30–50 for sync inference (short prompts, ~128 tokens).
- Peak batch jobs overnight: up to 400 requests/minute with longer sequences (~1024 tokens) for offline analytics.

3) Airgap constraints:
- Yes, fully air-gapped (no outbound internet). Software must be delivered as signed artifacts on FIPS-compliant USB drives or scannable media; internal change control approves packages only after checksum & signature verification.

4) Offline ops & upgrades:
- Maintenance windows: quarterly for major upgrades; monthly security patch windows for OS/firmware. For critical patches we can provide emergency windows.
- We require signed images and an upgrade runbook; we do not permit remote root access outside of scheduled sessions.

5) Network & bastion access:
- We can offer temporary bastion access during the initial install for a 4-hour window, monitored by our security team. For ongoing troubleshooting we prefer scheduled screen-share with our infra engineers.

I've attached our current network diagram and hardware inventory export for your reference (legacybank_onprem_network_v2.pdf, hardware_inventory.csv).

We are open to a 2-node POC to validate performance and the airgap upgrade process. Also: can Redwood provide signed upgrade artifacts and support HSM-based KMS integration? Pricing for the POC (including hardware validation support hours) is something we'll need to understand — please include discount options if applicable.

Regards,
John Hargreaves

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: On-prem air-gapped deployment — hardware & offline ops follow-up

Hi John — thanks for the details and the attachments (helpful). A few technical clarifications from the Redwood engineering side: 

- Signed artifacts & airgap upgrades: we support producing signed runtime artifacts (tarball + signature) and a deterministic install bundle. Our delivery options for airgapped sites include FIPS-compliant USB images or transfer via secure media. We will provide a verification tool (sha256 + signature verification) the infra team can run offline.

- HSM/KMS: Redwood supports integrating with customer HSMs (PKCS#11 compliant) for key wrapping and key management. We will need HSM endpoint details during POC setup.

- Install/upgrade model: initial install requires an engineer-led session with temporary bastion access (4h) or an on-site runbook-assisted install. Subsequent upgrades can be applied via the signed bundle and a lightweight agent that runs locally; the agent does not require outbound internet but does require the ability to accept a locally-mounted artifact.

- POC sizing: given your throughput targets, a 2-node POC with 3x H100 per node should allow us to validate latency for short requests and batch throughput for longer jobs. We'll instrument token-level metrics and a small eval set you provide.

- Power/cooling & racks: can you confirm power per rack (kW) and PDU type? Also rack U for the nodes. These affect our thermal/OS tuning recommendations.

Action items for us:
- I will draft a short POC SOW (2-node, 4-week technical validation) and include an option for on-site assistance during initial install.
- Marissa / Laura: can you please confirm pricing/discount guidance for a short POC?

Appreciate the speedy turnaround — happy to jump on the POC planning call next week.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Dev — that's exactly the level of detail we need. Quick replies: 
- Power/cooling: each rack can provide up to 20kW; PDUs are APC with SNMP disabled in the air-gapped zone. Nodes will be 2U each.
- POC: we agree to a 2-node, 4-week technical validation. Available dates: 6/7–6/11 (preferred) for the initial install window.
- POC pricing: we are budget-conscious — please include any standard POC discount and an estimated number of support hours for onboarding.
- Secure media: we can accept signed USB drives for delivery; please confirm Redwood will provide signed checksums and a verification tool.

Once Marissa confirms pricing guidance I will route the SOW through procurement.

Best,
John
